scope: This developer-source follow-up executes all three frozen selection-10 English recipes through unchanged production C++ and official sherpa2.0.1/ORT1.28.2 Windows libraries: 68 actual WAV jobs covering all54 Kokoro/one Piper/one Matcha voices, thirteen controls and info. Production Java performs157 checks, full import of nine distinct objects/eleven references, twelve actual children, independent settings, partial-synthesis cancellation, duration errors and recovery with zero network calls. An independent audit rereads394 raw files,82 protocol streams,74 WAVs and nine imported objects; original audio and labelled waveform media retain explicit host scope. Windows does not test Android liblog interposition or skipped-word rejection; quality, licenses, physical-phone/background and complete target10 remain unaccepted. APK inputs/bytes are unchanged. The earlier metadata/source follow-up verifies eleven trained Nano assets, seven actual production-C++ WAV jobs plus seven controls, forty production Java/native checks, and independently rereads original outputs/imported objects. A user-importable pinned manifest and actual HOST audio/waveform media are supplied without changing APK inputs or bytes. Host ORT 1.28.0/API28 remains distinct from production Android 1.28.2/API28; phone, SAF, quality and endurance are untested. Development APK dev.24 corrects diffusion callback phases to loading/generating without changing model math; it includes signed explicit runtime association plans, hardlink reuse and independently managed source/runtime models, alongside user-selected native asset preparation and shared queued jobs. This checkpoint adds actual trained SD1.5 CPU host generation, sampler cancellation/recovery and A/B/A output checks using unchanged production C++ inference with a Windows-only parent-lifetime port. It also retains isolated T5 F32 staging and adds old-LTX publisher-modulation observations and native diagnostics; both new B sampling conditions still fail frozen latent gates. The full F32 candidate passes case A but fails case B; neither it nor the sampler diagnostics are registered or packaged. Two signed preparation programs and nine audited model-free architecture graphs are packaged without learned model data. The production Java core performed one full trained host preparation with 20 verified outputs; Android Service, SAF, converter execution and background endurance remain untested. The original signing identity is preserved. Packaged SoulX and other existing App engine contracts retain their scoped records; complete trained SoulX host speech is separate from quality, public user acquisition and Android acceptance. Retained old-LTX evidence records three real-prompt single-scale trained HOST video jobs with explicit Google/community Q5 T5, original 0.9.8 distilled DiT/VAE, independent original-forward comparison and actual RGB/MP4 media. Frozen full-chain float gates remain failed despite passing RGB gates; numerical acceptance is false. Separate tensor/T5/DiT/VAE Android compilation is not App registration or phone execution. Official default multi-scale/PixArt text-weight identity, video quality, complete public assets and target-17 Android acceptance remain open. Older component receipts retain their original scope. App updates deliver foundation code only; users explicitly select/manage all model assets, with no automatic model retrieval. One complete v0.3.0 still requires F-01-F-12, existing text, selections 01-14/16/17 and every frozen subtarget, trained quality/resources, physical-phone load/unload/screen-off/API/upgrade evidence and A1-A11/R01-R05. No complete Release, physical-device acceptance or all-selected-model support is claimed.
